newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - AEGON IN MEGA U.S. TAKEOVER.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - AEGON IN MEGA U.S. TAKEOVER.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon said on Monday it was buying the insurance activities of Providian Corp of the United States in a deal worth $3.5 billion.
The takeover is the biggest U.S. life insurance purchase to date and the biggest U.S. acquisition by a Dutch company. It is likely to be finalised by the middle of next year.
The deal is one the largest in a rapidly consolidating global life-insurance industry which is pressured by high costs and tough competition from banks and mutual funds all chasing consumer savings.

"Consolidation in the insurance sector will certainly continue in Europe and the United States. Market shares are diminishing and European union will accelerate this process," said Dutch-based IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen.
Aegon said the deal, which moves it into the top three European insurance players and promotes it to number 11 in the United States, would involve a tax-free share swap.
Providian shareholders would receive Aegon stock worth $2.62 billion, equivalent to $28/share, and Aegon USA would assume loans worth $780 million and preferred stock worth $100 million.
Providian stockholders will also receive shares in Providian Bancorp which will be spun off as an independent company.
"We weren't interested in the banking side. We want to stay with our core (insurance) business," Aegon chairman Kees Storm told reporters.
Aegon said the acquisition would increase earnings by around five percent in 1998.
"In the first full (consolidated) year, 1998, the increase in earnings per share...could be around five percent," a spokesman told Reuters.

"This record-setting acquisition is fully in line with Aegon's stated strategy. It is earnings enhancing, highly compatible and will provide a healthy boost to our growth into the next century," Storm said.
He added that the group's USA division's profit margin should increase because of the deal which was effectively a hedge against interest rate changes.
"It's a weapon against the influence of changes in interest rates. When they rise it's good for our home services, but not so good for other units," Storm said.
Analysts welcomed the deal, particularly the swift knock-on effect on earnings per share.
"This is a very positive acquisition. Looking at the EPS, we expect an increase of between four and eight percent," said Van der Feen, who maintained a buy rating on Aegon stock.
"One of the main points is that the deal is to be mainly financed internally without a major share issue," he added.
Aegon's Storm also signalled further acquisitions, should the right opportunities come along.
"I don't exclude further acquisitions. We have one to 1.5 billion guilders and we've set no limits on ourselves," he said.
"If we see possibilities, for example, in Spain, we'll do it. If it's small, we can pay with our own capital. If a bigger opportunity comes up, we'll make use of the capital markets."
Aegon shares jumped on the news, adding 8.00 guilders or over eight percent to 107.20 guilders on an otherwise quietly firm Amsterdam bourse.

Kentucky-based Providian, which employs 8,600 staff, is active throughout the United States, operating in four divisions -- Providian Bancorp, Direct Insurance Group, Agency Group and Capital Management Group. The group is capitalised at just under $5.0 billion.

The Hague-based Aegon, with a global workforce of almost 20,000, has total assets of around 150 billion guilders and operates in the Netherlands, the United States, Britain, Spain and Hungary. The market values Aegon at some 26.3 billion guilders.
